beats.t: Beyond the western gate lay a market. Starlight tents stood in rows, with tiny stars hanging from poles instead of lanterns.
At its center, customers crowded one particularly shabby tent. Crooked letters read: Compatibility · Naming · Wayfinding. Credit accepted.
Credit accepted. Definitely him.
Only one person would write that sign.
Inside, a man with a glove on his right hand read a young star woman's palm. Her face blushed with starlight.
Look at this line. A benefactor comes from the west. Very close, too. May I ask your birth date and time?
Just as she opened her mouth, Neo stood before the tent. A silver cloak swayed behind the shoulders blocking its entrance.
Customers from the west. These ones aren't taking a free consultation.
The gloved hand froze in midair. The man slowly looked up and met Yeoni's eyes.
Yundal. You said you'd secure a spot. You really did.
The smile left Yundal's face. Not even surprise. As though something had caught in his throat.
...You know my name?
Of course. Yundal. Right-hand glove. Compatibility scams.
Over there, everyone forgot after a day. Luna, her sister. Every morning, a first-time customer.
Yeoni took out the notebook and opened its first page before him. Their handwriting lay there. Yundal · Right-hand glove · Compatibility scams.
I wrote it down, afraid I'd forget. They said the air here erased memories, so I wrote faster than they disappeared.
Yundal stared at the line, tracing the letters with a gloved finger. At compatibility scams, his mouth lifted as though collapsing.
Of all things to survive, compatibility scams. That's a business loss.
It's true.
That makes it hurt more. You haven't changed, my lady.
She's already gone. Don't blame me for losing your customer.
The young star woman glanced between them and left. Without ever paying for her palm reading.
Mr. Cat hasn't changed, either. You're responsible for this month's sales.
Then a savory smell came from behind the tent. Charcoal, sizzling oil. Yeoni's stomach reacted first.
Pig. Followed your nose, didn't you? Still a pig's nose.
Moka?! Why are you here? You said festival island!
I went. Then this con artist chased me there by boat. Said a guide needed someone to cook.
It's true. Star people eat light. After three days of hunger, I started thinking of otter skewers.
So I came to collect his tab. Thirty skewers he owes.
You came to another sky to collect that?
Thirty skewers is serious money. And I'm still not used to you being human.
I'm human now. Not a pig.
Still a pig. A pig at heart. Same face when someone hands you a skewer.
Grumbling, Moka pushed one into Yeoni's hand. Starlight mushrooms and unknown fruit on a stick. Flavor. Warmth.
Delicious. Just like the first one on the Island of Expression.
...Obviously. My skewers taste good even when the sky changes.
With that, Moka whipped his head away. His tail swished fiercely behind him. Only the tail could hide nothing.
Otter. Good to see you.
Good, nothing. Neo, what's with your hand? It's black.
Everyone looked at Neo's right hand. The stain had passed his wrist. He pulled down his sleeve.
Cut a few black hands on the way. Must have rubbed off then.
More than that, I think. Let's discuss it over the chart.
Yundal cleared the tent's table. A twelve-part board was engraved on it, the same shape Yeoni had seen on the phone.
This sky's map. A destiny chart. Each square is a room in a life.
(Eight characters in the Four Pillars. Twelve rooms here.)
You needn't memorize all the rooms. We're entering only one today.
Twelve rooms must be hard to clean.
That's why most people leave one or two messy.
Yundal pointed with a gloved finger to one space, marked 寅. The very star name Yeoni had seen on the phone shone there.
[ Life Palace: Yin (寅) · Lian Zhen · Bright ]
Your room. Its ruling star is Lian Zhen, the Prison Star that confines itself.
Confines? Am I trapped?
You're the one confining. A star holding fire, gripping it tightly for fear it will burn someone else.
Yeoni could not answer. Moments when Hurting Officer erupted came back. The courtroom. Neo's scorched hand. Since then, Yeoni had shut their mouth every time they wanted to shout.
(A star holding on. Right. Lately, I'm always holding it in.)
What does the pig hold? Always giving everything away.
That's Lian Zhen. In light, principles; in darkness, a prison.
It says bright now.
For now.
Yundal took out a small pouch and shook it. Four handfuls of colored dust fell onto the chart. Gold, red, blue. And black.
Stars can carry four tags. Born in a 壬 year, you get these.
Gold dust settled on a star in the Children room beside the Money room. Red on the great star in Money. Blue on a small star in the room of outside journeys.
[ Prosperity Transformation: Tian Liang · Authority Transformation: Zi Wei · Distinction Transformation: Zuo Fu · Obstruction Transformation: Wu Qu ]
The other three are good. The problem is the last.
The black dust fell last. The Work room, marked 午, Wu. Two great stars stood side by side. It clung to one, then seeped into the chart.
The black one. Same space that spread on my phone.
Obstruction is a place blocked because it never received what was due. It's the name Black Moon uses in this sky.
Even the name's gloomy.
Attached to Wu Qu. A Metal star.
The tent fell quiet. Yeoni slowly looked at Neo. He wasn't watching the chart. He watched one part of the sky beyond the tent.
Metal? Neo is Metal too. 庚.
Coincidence.
Few coincidences in this sky. That space is Influence. As for who Influence is in your chart…
Enough.
Neo's voice lowered. Yundal fell silent, his eyes fixed on Neo's sleeve.
(Officer. Influence. In the library, Yundal said Neo was my Influence. Then what the black thing is after...)
Yundal suggested her room first. You couldn't know a room's smell until you entered it yourself.
The Yin gate stood on the palace's east side. Beyond it was a round room, mirrors covering every wall.
All me. Little me, middle-school me, last year's me.
Every reflected Yeoni gripped something. At seven, tears. At fifteen, an exam paper. Last year, an upturned umbrella.
Every mirror Yeoni wore a flower pin too. Only last year's Yeoni had all five petals red.
All holding something. Could just let go.
Holding on because letting go might mean losing it.
A red lantern floated at the center. Inside, a flame fluttered like a bird in an iron cage. Its edges were dark red.
“So it's you. The owner of my room.” A low, hoarse woman's voice came from the lantern.
Are you... Lian Zhen?
“Some call me that. Others call me Prison. You've learned to cage your fire.”
Yes. Someone gets hurt when I shout.
“Good. Fire that knows confinement doesn't burn others. But remember: fire only confined will rot.”
The mirror held by last year's Yeoni cracked. Black water seeped through and ran along its frame to the floor.
Black again. Why, when this is my room?
Three directions. Your room in 寅, career in 午, money in 戌 form a triangle.
Plain words, con artist!
Fire next door fills our room with smoke, too.
Say that first.
Black water crawled toward the lantern. The flame curled inward. Layers of red light went dark, one after another.
“Child. The Wu room. My sibling star is crying there. The Metal star.”
Wu Qu?
“The black thing clings to that star and eats its Metal. Once it has eaten it all, it will seek something that resembles Metal.”
Yeoni turned. Neo stood before a mirror. In the reflection, the stain reached his elbow. In reality, it was still below the wrist.
Neo. Your hand in the mirror. It's blacker.
Mirrors sometimes show what comes next. Then it's still ahead.
Don't say still!
Hurting Officer's fire surged to Yeoni's throat. They clenched their teeth and swallowed it. At that moment, Neo's right hand twitched.
...Sorry. I shouldn't shout.
It's fine. That much only tickles.
Last-year me. Let that go. I said let go.
Last year's Yeoni gripped the umbrella harder. More black water poured through the crack.
(Tell her to let go, and she grips harder. I did too.)
Give it to me. I'll hold it.
Yeoni reached into the mirror and accepted the inside-out umbrella. It smelled of rain from that day.
The black water stopped. It cleared, then quietly flowed out along the frame.
'What is blocked flows when received. You have just received what was yours.'
That's how Obstruction turns toward Prosperity. When someone receives it, the blocked place flows.
Then if someone receives what's in 午 too…
In theory.
Dampness lingered in her palm. Wiping couldn't dry it. The other mirror Yeonis still clutched something.
Inside the lantern, Lian Zhen seemed about to speak, then stopped. That silence felt strangely heavy to Yeoni.
Outside, the palace square was unsettled. Gray-faced star people walked in a line toward somewhere, carrying unlit lanterns.
Where is everyone going?
Toward Wu. The Work room.
Yundal's gloved right hand pulled that way on its own. Something beneath it sucked in air. With his left hand, he gripped his right wrist tightly.
Urgh... Happens when Black Moon's close. The hole knows first.
Yundal, your hand.
I'm fine. Act hurt in front of customers, and sales drop.
That's my line.
Learned it from you, Mr. Cat.
Then a metallic voice rang from the colonnade's end, accompanied by a hammer striking a judgment bench.
“Judgment. All who enter this sky's Work room, all who sing, all who laugh: everything confiscated.”
Moka dropped his skewer. Metal clanged against stone. His whiskers trembled.
Moka? What's wrong?
...That voice. I know it. Since before it became a crow.
